drivers.derivation: Impressions = daily users (DAP) x impressions per user. DAP: Meta added about 0.10B people in the year to Sep-2026 (3.54 -> 3.64B), about 40% of the ~240M people who came online worldwide in 2025 (ITU, src 32; 2.2B still offline). No published forecast of Meta's users exists and ITU publishes no forward path, so the build assumes Meta keeps adding about 0.025B a quarter (judgment, carded with the alternatives) (3.67B Dec-2026, 3.77B Dec-2027, 3.87B Dec-2028, 3.97B Dec-2029), so user growth slows from ~3% to ~2.6% a year as the base grows. Impressions per user grew +10.3% / +14.4% / +10.7% / +6.8% y/y from Q4-25 to Q3-26 (impressions over DAP growth): the 2025 ad-load launches (WhatsApp Status and Threads ads) are now in the base, so the Q3 call credits engagement and 'ad load optimizations' rather than new surfaces (src 31). Engagement: Instagram time per user at an all-time high and up double digits, Facebook Reels time up double digits, Threads time per user +20%, Q3 ranking launches added +4% to Reels time (src 31). Path for impressions per user: +5.0% in Q4-26 and 2027, +4.5% in 2028, +4.0% in 2029. The call gives engagement evidence (time spent and ranking gains) but no figure for future ad load, so this is a judgment between engagement-only growth (+3%) and the Q3-2026 figure (+6.8%), carded. With ad revenue set by the market build (ppa_idx), impressions mainly split ad revenue into volume and price. Result: impressions +7.5% Q4-26, +7.9% to +8.8% across 2027 quarters (Q1 is high because Mar-2026 DAP dipped), ~+7.3% in 2028, ~+6.7% in 2029; year means 112.6 / 121.9 / 130.8 / 139.6.

With ad revenue set by the market build (ppa_idx), impressions mainly split ad revenue into volume and price. judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: Ad revenue 2027-29: grow with the social ad market, or keep gaining share?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: This sets FoA ad revenue for 2027-29, the biggest input in the model. The base round used price-per-ad steps of +10% / +7% / +4%, and the gate found nothing to support them. The set now grows ad revenue with the social ad market at a constant Meta share: WARC +14.6% in 2027 and at least +10.6% in 2028, Omdia 12% a year to 2030. That gives ads of $286B / $317B / $355B. It is a call because Meta grew 5.7 points faster than the market in 2026 and no source forecasts Meta's own share.

options.label: Market growth, share held (set)
options.reasoning: Rests on published market forecasts (WARC Q3-2026, Omdia) and assumes no further share gain, the moderately conservative base case when no source sizes Meta's share.

options.label: Middle: half of 2026's share gain, fading
options.reasoning: Meta's 2026 lead over the market (ranking and ad performance gains) partly continues: +2.85pt over WARC in 2027, +1.4pt in 2028, then market growth (Omdia) in 2029; ads about +17.5% / +12% / +12%.

options.label: Share gain continues at 2026's pace
options.reasoning: Meta took share in 2026 (+27% vs social +21.3%) on ranking and ad performance gains; repeating that 5.7-point gap each year gives ads about +20% / +16% / +18%.

options.label: KeyBanc: low-to-mid-20% growth through 2028
options.reasoning: The one post-print sell-side growth view: KeyBanc expects AI product momentum to keep revenue growing in the low-to-mid 20s through 2028 (ads +22% in 2027-28 here).

judgment_calls_for_kilian.why: It is the only path anchored on published forecasts for these years; share-gain cases rest on 2026 repeating or on one analyst's view.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: FoA costs 2027-29: keep the slowing cash-cost path, or price in costs staying high?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: foa_margin is the Family of Apps operating margin after D&A. D&A now comes from the depreciation engine. The cash-cost part keeps the base round's path: cash costs ex one-offs up 20% / 12.5% / 5% a year, with headcount 12% lower after the May 2026 cut (66k at Q3) and Reality Labs spending moved to AI. The Q3 call gives no 2027 budget. It names infrastructure (third-party cloud, depreciation, data center costs) and AI token costs as the expense drivers and says Meta will 'continue investing aggressively'. The gate marked the cost path unsupported.

options.label: Keep the slowing cost path (set)
options.reasoning: Headcount is 12% lower after the May 2026 cut and RL spending was moved to AI; first-party Muse models cut content processing costs by more than 80% (call), so cost growth can slow as revenue grows.

options.label: Costs stay high: margin -1.6pt 2027, -2.0pt 2028-29
options.reasoning: Third-party cloud and AI token costs scale with AI usage: Meta AI engagement per person more than doubled since April, and more than 10 million people in the US and Canada set up Muse personal agents in a month and a half (Mark Zuckerberg, CEO, Q3 call), and the call says spending stays aggressive.

options.label: Depreciation from the 11-17 audit fit (lower D&A)
options.reasoning: The 11-17 two-class fit put buildings at ~10 years with no check against construction in progress; it gives lower 2028-29 D&A. Shown for completeness: the 10-K's 25-30-year building life and the CIP balances contradict it.

options.label: Server life cut to 5 years from 2027
options.reasoning: Amazon cut a subset of servers from six to five years in 2025 because AI hardware turns over faster; the same move at Meta adds about $5-7B a year of D&A.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.why: The headcount cut and the RL shift are booked facts; the cost-up case is real but Meta can steer AI usage costs with its own models. The D&A options are listed because they size over 5%, not because the evidence favors them.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: Impressions per user 2027-29: +5% / +4.5% / +4% (set), engagement-only +3%, or the Q3-2026 +6.8%?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: Impressions are daily users times impressions per user. Users add about 0.025B a quarter, roughly Meta's 2026 capture of new internet users (ITU). Impressions per user grow from engagement (Instagram and Facebook Reels time up double digits, Threads +20% per user) and ad load. Q3-2026 ran +6.8%, after the 2025 ad-load launches dropped out of the comparison. No source forecasts either part, so the gate marked both as unsupported. With ad revenue set by the market build, this mostly splits ads into volume and price.

options.label: +5% / +4.5% / +4% (set)
options.reasoning: Between the engagement evidence on the call and the Q3-2026 figure; fades as time-spent gains get harder on a larger base.

options.label: +3% a year (engagement only)
options.reasoning: No new ad surfaces: impressions per user grow only with time spent.

options.label: +6.8% a year (Q3-2026 figure)
options.reasoning: Ad load optimizations keep adding at the 2026 rate.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.why: Midway between the two evidence points; the effect stays under 5% either way.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: Capex 2027-29: $241B / $250B / $250B (set), or the low or high post-print estimate?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: FY2027 capex ($241.3B) is the mean of the three estimates published after the Q3 print, and FY2028 ($250B) is Morgan Stanley's bar. No one publishes FY2029. The set takes a plateau, citing Jefferies' view that the AI capex cycle 'may have peaked' and Morgan Stanley's 'downward bias' flag for 2028. Each option is sized with its knock-on effects: the depreciation engine re-runs D&A and the net debt roll re-runs interest on that capex path.

options.label: $250B plateau (set)
options.reasoning: Jefferies sees a possible peak or mid-cycle correction and MS flags downward bias for 2028.

options.label: +10% in 2029
options.reasoning: MS's exhibit total still rises in 2028; AI demand keeps capex growing.

options.label: -10% in 2029
options.reasoning: A mid-cycle correction in 2029, the risk Jefferies names after its 2028 plateau; spending falls to about $225B.

options.label: $225B in 2027 (Morgan Stanley, lowest post-print)
options.reasoning: The lowest of the three post-print estimates.

options.label: ~$250B in 2027 (Wedbush, Wells Fargo)
options.reasoning: The two highest post-print estimates: Wedbush raised its 2027 estimate from $210B to $249B and Wells Fargo expects about $250B after the Q3 call.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.why: FY2029 sits outside the horizon window, so the level matters only through net debt and the FY2029 terms.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: FoA other revenue 2027-29 ($7.0B / $10.5B / $14.3B): keep, messaging only, or more subscription revenue?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: WhatsApp paid messaging plus subscriptions (Meta One, global from September 2026, 15M+ subscriptions and trials). Meta gives no outlook or subscriber data, so the gate marked the path a trend. Value effect is under 1%.

options.label: Keep $7.0B / $10.5B / $14.3B (set)
options.reasoning: Messaging growth slowing from +59% plus a subscription ramp.

options.label: Messaging only (~21% lower)
options.reasoning: Business messaging keeps growing but Meta One adds no paid subscription ramp, so FY2027-29 other revenue is 0.786x the set (FY2027 about $5.5B, each year about 21% lower); Q4-26 is unchanged.

options.label: Meta One full year at ~$4 (+10%)
options.reasoning: 15M subscriptions at a ~$4 blended price add ~$0.7B a year.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: Reality Labs loss 2028-29 ($13.5B / $12.5B) and revenue: keep, no cut, or faster cut?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: RL is valued separately (a venture value), so its loss and revenue reach the target only through cash. FY2026 and FY2027 rest on Meta's guides (declared). Nothing sizes 2028-29, so the gate marked it unsupported.

options.label: Keep $13.5B / $12.5B (set)
options.reasoning: Continues the narrowing Meta guided for 2027.

options.label: No cut: ~$18.5B a year
options.reasoning: Reality Labs spending stays at the 2026 level because Meta keeps funding VR, glasses and wearables at the current rate.

options.label: Faster cut: $12B / $10B / $8B

value.name: Class C ATM program (planned ~$60B), earlier start 2027-05-15
